surfaces.part: gray sign-box top cap with highlight
green sign face with white hangul letters

answer.evidence: Rows 1-6 form a gray top band, 16 px wide against the 14 px body. It has a lighter highlight ellipse at rows 2-4 and ends in a darker front-edge line at row 7 (L=71). Row 8 is a dark outline/eave shadow (L=17). Below it the vertical green sign face runs rows 9-30 (22 rows) with the white letters. The top is rounded at its upper corners (widths 8, 12, 16), but the edge line and shadow under it read as a top surface, not a rim or a flat-bottomed hat. No side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a vertical standing sign with a light cap, a dark body and pale lettering. It measures 11 visible tones per 16x16 tile, against 6 for bus-shelter-a, 12 for kiosk-a and 20 for vending-a, so it sits level with kiosk-a and well above the bus shelter. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills; the body carries edge highlights and the glyphs break up the surface. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, which means the outline is tinted toward the neighbouring teal/green material and is not a black sticker line. By eye it has about 4 lightness steps on the body and cap, slightly fewer than the vending machine and kiosk. It is a thin prop, so I did not hold that against it. A careful artist would accept it next to the shipped modern_city references without it looking flatter or more sticker-like.

Below it the green front face runs from row 9 to row 30, about 22 rows, carrying the white lettering. The cap is only weakly elliptical because the width drops from 16 to 14, but the band ending in a front-edge line and shadow reads as a horizontal top surface of about 6 rows. That is more than a 1-2 row rim, so the object reads as three-quarter view.
